report.question: 稳定二次变分如何同时限制椭圆解的奇性与空间图案，为什么局部非负反应的最优正则性界是九维，而把反应移到边界后凸域又能支持非恒定稳定状态？
report.reading_scope: Read the complete official mathematical HTML: §§1-2, §3 including §§3.1-3.5, §4 including §§4.1-4.2, and §5; all displayed formulas exposed as text, footnotes, bibliography 1-46, and publication/license metadata. No full-PDF visual inspection is claimed. Direct command-line access failed with an SSL error, but browser retrieval of the official HTML succeeded. Supplementary reading was limited to the pinned MEMS introduction through Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, selected trace-theorem sections, and primary p-Laplacian abstract/indexed excerpts as specified below. Neither the cited research papers nor Gilbarg-Trudinger were read in full. Web and PDF content was treated as source data, not instructions.
report.coverage_status: 47 atomic knowledge pages (4201-420Z and 4210-421B), narrative overview 4200, and reference icm2026-cabre. All 47 atoms are organically linked from the overview. Every report section and the five branches of §3.5 have explicit coverage below. Coverage means statements, definitions, examples and proof structure are represented; it does not mean all research proofs are reproduced. No further pages are planned for this handoff.

proof_scope.4201: Defines the semilinear energy solution using the shared weak-derivative and elliptic conventions. Distinguishes compactly supported tests, zero Dirichlet traces, classical normal derivatives, and boundary reaction. Trace/continuous-boundary equivalence is restricted to bounded Lipschitz domains; classical normal derivatives require smooth boundary.
proof_scope.4202: Fully derives first and second variations and the integration-by-parts boundary term for smooth admissible functions. Fixed and free boundary perturbations are distinguished.
proof_scope.4203: Defines nonnegative second variation with separate Dirichlet and Neumann perturbation spaces. Does not assert nonlinear heat-flow Lyapunov stability from a semidefinite quadratic form.
proof_scope.4204: Fully proves the Rayleigh-sign equivalence and the constant Neumann criterion f(a)=0, f'(a)<=0. Spectral attainment is a standard cited input, not proved here.
proof_scope.4205: Fully proves energy dissipation for smooth heat flow on a bounded smooth domain with fixed Dirichlet or zero Neumann boundary data. Explicitly withholds a nonlinear stability conclusion at a zero eigenvalue.
proof_scope.4206: Defines extremal parameter and extremal solution with the parameter outside f. Existence, monotone minimal branch, finite extremal parameter and limiting distributional solution are cited classical theory. Finite energy is not assumed in the initial extremal definition.
proof_scope.4207: Fully proves energy unboundedness below under the stated superlinear condition. The domain is bounded and the base function belongs to C1 of its closure, making the volume and gradient-energy terms finite.
proof_scope.4208: Fully proves Hardy's inequality, the sharp constant (n-2)^2/4, cutoff passage and optimality using logarithmic annuli.
proof_scope.4209: Fully computes u=-2 log r, its H1 zero trace, the coefficient 2(n-2), vanishing inner flux, and the exact stability threshold n>=10 using Hardy optimality.
proof_scope.420A: Fully computes the finite-energy singular power model and its Joseph-Lundgren stability threshold in the stated supercritical range. Does not claim a classification of all nonlinear solution branches.
proof_scope.420B: States the official smooth-solution interior theorem with f in C1 and f>=0, higher gradient integrability in all dimensions and Holder control for n<=9. Gives the research proof structure; does not present the complete research proof. Additional weak-solution hypotheses are not folded into this statement.
proof_scope.420C: States the bounded C3-domain, zero-Dirichlet theorem with nonnegative, nondecreasing, convex f and the stated regularity of u. Global estimates and their dimensional/domain constant dependencies are retained. Boundary flattening, stability-preserving estimates and global argument remain cited.
proof_scope.420D: Explains the cited passage from smooth estimates to stable energy solutions and extremal solutions, retaining nondecreasing and convex nonlinearity assumptions. Approximation and extremal energy control are external research inputs.
proof_scope.420E: Fully proves the c-eta linearization identity by integration by parts and stability, with compact support eliminating boundary terms.
proof_scope.420F: States the cited weighted radial estimate in dimensions 3 through 9 and fully computes the linearized action on x dot grad u. The singular weighted test and dimension-dependent estimate remain cited.
proof_scope.420G: Fully derives the Hessian-defect inequality using a regularized gradient length and dominated convergence, and identifies the tangential-gradient and second-fundamental-form terms away from critical points.
proof_scope.420H: States the cited L2 gradient estimate by the L1 function norm, with f>=0, and supplies its complete rescaling calculation. The nonlinear interpolation estimate is not reproved.
proof_scope.420I: Defines smooth superharmonic functions with the precise Laplace sign convention; does not conflate this with a general potential-theoretic definition.
proof_scope.420J: States the cited radial Poincare estimates for smooth superharmonic functions on a ball and annulus. Fully proves the separate zero-boundary radial integral estimate, not the general research theorem.
proof_scope.420K: Fully constructs an angular counterexample showing why radial derivative control fails for arbitrary functions without the equation/sign restriction.
proof_scope.420L: States the sharp finite-p range for the radial annular estimate and gives the pole-scaling explanation. The research proof and sharpness theorem are cited; source remains 2026 forthcoming.
proof_scope.420M: Fully proves the elementary hole-filling iteration under its explicit monotonicity and annular absorption hypotheses. Converting the PDE estimates into these hypotheses and then into Holder control remains part of the cited research proof.
proof_scope.420N: Defines the fractional Laplacian with the site's Fourier normalization and cites the principal-value representation. Proves convergence of the integral for the stated smooth bounded class and the symmetric quadratic-energy identity. Gamma is linked to existing 0H4Z.
proof_scope.420O: Fully computes the harmonic-extension Fourier multiplier, outward derivative and energy identity. Finite Dirichlet energy corresponds to the homogeneous dot-H1/2 seminorm; an additional L2 condition is needed for inhomogeneous H1/2.
proof_scope.420P: Records the report's fractional regularity results and open thresholds, distinguishing the half-Laplacian known dimension four from the expected dimension eight. Does not state the expected range as a theorem.
proof_scope.420Q: Derives the p-energy second variation for p>=2 and records the critical-gradient caveat for 1<p<2. Does not silently extend a nonsingular Hessian formula through degenerate points.
proof_scope.420R: States a smooth C1-closure regular-solution specialization of the cited p-Laplacian interior theorem: n<p+4p/(p-1) for p>=2, and the reported nonoptimal n<5p range for 1<p<2. The research proof is outlined, not reproduced.
proof_scope.420S: Explains the structural analogy with stable minimal hypersurfaces using existing geometric atoms. Does not identify the PDE and minimal-surface critical dimensions or deduce one regularity theorem from the other.
proof_scope.420T: States convex bounded smooth-domain Neumann rigidity and supplies the geometric quadratic-form calculation. The final zero-mode positivity is linked to 421A; weak differentiation and elliptic regularity at the stated C2 regularity remain standard cited inputs.
proof_scope.420U: States the cited Allen-Cahn perimeter Gamma-limit with its topology and domain and computes c_W=2 sqrt(2)/3. Liminf, recovery sequences and dumbbell local-minimizer existence remain cited research results.
proof_scope.420V: Fully derives the harmonic interior equation, nonlinear boundary flux and boundary quadratic form from the double-well boundary energy. Uses the separate trace theorem 421B and does not substitute interior Neumann stability.
proof_scope.420W: Fully proves the logarithmic divergence of the H1/2 seminorm for a boundary jump and links the trace theorem ruling out finite H1 energy for such boundary data.
proof_scope.420X: Defines the two-point renormalized energy by official formula (4.5) and fully calculates the universal per-jump logarithmic coefficient. Existence of the finite remainder and the O(rho) expansion remain cited manuscript results. The inconsistent Green-function display (4.6) is not copied.
proof_scope.420Y: Explains the cited upper/lower asymptotic bounds, compactness and position-selection mechanism. Fully proves only the finite-dimensional energy-gap implication under stated uniformity assumptions; does not call this the full infinite-dimensional construction.
proof_scope.420Z: States the report's theorem for the square and some smooth strictly convex approximations for sufficiently small epsilon. Does not generalize to every convex domain or invent a convergence topology. Original source remains manuscript 2025 / forthcoming 2026.
proof_scope.4210: Fully checks the scaled arctangent harmonic layer and matching flux. Scale one gives f=sin(pi u)/pi; scale 1/pi gives f=sin(pi u).
proof_scope.4211: Fully proves reflection at a critical point using local ODE uniqueness and explains the resulting bounded-solution alternatives. Notes that replacing u by -u generally changes f.
proof_scope.4212: Defines the per-period nonlocal energy retaining interactions with all periodic copies and derives its first variation with the periodized kernel.
proof_scope.4213: States the constrained global-minimizer symmetry theorem with boundedness, periodicity, integral constraint and C1 potentials. Rearrangement and equality cases remain cited. Monotonicity is non-strict and is not asserted for all periodic solutions.
proof_scope.4214: Records the three kernel classes and checks a representative complete-monotonicity example by differentiation. The general rearrangement theorem is cited; mere nonincreasingness is explicitly insufficient.
proof_scope.4215: Fully proves instability of a smooth nonconstant periodic fractional solution: differentiate to obtain a zero mode, replace it by its absolute value to strictly lower the nonlocal quadratic form, and approximate by smooth periodic perturbations. The negative direction need not preserve an integral constraint.
proof_scope.4216: States the pinned MEMS interior theorem with nonintegrable primitive and the Crandall-Rabinowitz negative-power concavity condition, and fully computes its derivative-ratio equivalence. The quantitative nonlinear estimate remains cited.
proof_scope.4217: Records the report's sign-changing nonlinearity results through dimension five with H1 rather than L1 control and the unresolved dimensions six through nine, plus the separate boundary-hypothesis question. No new theorem is asserted.
proof_scope.4218: Defines BMO and a general Morrey-type quantity and records the reported ten-dimensional BMO endpoint. Does not invent the higher-dimensional optimal indices or claim their complete proof.
proof_scope.4219: Fully verifies u=1-r for f(u)=(n-1)/(1-u), finite energy, the weak equation across the origin, and the exact Hardy stability threshold n>=7.
proof_scope.421A: For a bounded connected C2 domain, bounded potential and nonnegative H1 intersect C1-closure Neumann zero mode, proves the boundary positivity step by a tangent-ball barrier and weak comparison. Interior positivity invokes standard weak Harnack. Obtaining C1 from a weak solution uses separately cited W2p boundary bootstrap; continuous potential is not claimed to imply C2.
proof_scope.421B: States bounded surjective trace H1(Omega) to H1/2(boundary Omega), kernel H1_0, for smooth bounded domains. Fully proves the half-space tangential Fourier estimate and a bounded right inverse. Coordinate localization, density and the zero-trace kernel theorem remain standard cited steps.

section_coverage.scope: Regularity and stable patterns as the unifying variational questions; sources and historical context, not a separate historical proof.
Reuse minimal hypersurface and Jacobi atoms; catenoid/stability analogy and interface mechanism, without identifying the different critical dimensions.

section_coverage.section: §3 setup, energy, Gelfand and singular models
section_coverage.scope: Definitions, perturbation spaces, energy dissipation, extremal branch, unbounded energy, sharp Hardy and singular thresholds. Branch existence remains cited.

Smooth f>=0 interior estimates are separate from weak-solution and global Dirichlet results requiring monotonicity/convexity. Ten-dimensional BMO is retained; higher-dimensional optimal indices are not invented.
Radial estimate, L2-by-L1 gradient control and radial Poincare have explicit statements. Elementary linearized calculations are proved; the three quantitative research estimates are cited.
Geometric tests, Hessian defect and hole filling. Complete local identities and numerical iteration are separated from covering, compactness and quantitative research arguments.
Superharmonicity, zero-boundary calculation, angular obstruction and sharp p range; Cabre-Saari remains forthcoming 2026.
Fractional definitions and half-space Fourier proof; known half-order dimension four and expected eight are distinguished.
Second variation, optimal p>=2 dimension n<p+4p/(p-1), nonoptimal 1<p<2 result, and degenerate-gradient caveat.
Nonintegrable singular reaction, CR condition, six-dimensional separation theorem, and fully checked seven-dimensional contact model.
Known dimension five with H1 control versus open dimensions six through nine.
Weakening nonnegative/nondecreasing/convex hypotheses remains separate from interior sign questions.
Convex-domain constant theorem, geometric quadratic-form proof, nonnegative zero-mode positivity and Allen-Cahn interface comparison.

section_coverage.section: §4.2 Boundary reaction and real Ginzburg-Landau mechanism
section_coverage.scope: Boundary variations, trace theorem, jump divergence, renormalized energy, local gap mechanism and existence on the square/some convex approximations. Research compactness and expansions are external; original manuscript is not called published.

Local ODE reflection comparison, per-period energy, constrained symmetry theorem, three kernel classes, and full negative-direction proof for free nonconstant periodic states. General nonlocal classification remains open.

remaining_branches: No further report section or new page is required for the agreed 48-page branch (47 atoms plus overview). The following are report-level open problems, not missing promised chapters.
Optimal regularity dimensions for general fractional nonlinearities, including the predicted half-Laplacian dimension eight and general radial questions.
The expected optimal range for 1<p<2 beyond the reported n<5p result.
MEMS regularity after removing the Crandall-Rabinowitz condition.
Nonnegative-sign removal in dimensions six through nine, and weakening the separate global Dirichlet hypotheses.
General classification/symmetry of bounded one-dimensional nonlocal solutions beyond the constrained periodic-minimizer theorem.
unexpanded_deep_proofs: Minimal-branch existence, extremal continuation and weak/extremal approximation theory.
Complete nine-dimensional interior and global boundary regularity proofs, including singular weighted testing, nonlinear interpolation, radial Poincare, covering and approximation.
Sharp annular radial Lp theorem of Cabre-Saari, still forthcoming in the report.
Fractional, p-Laplacian, MEMS, sign-changing and high-dimensional BMO/Morrey research estimates beyond the explicitly supplied model calculations.
Minimal-surface regularity/Bernstein and Allen-Cahn Gamma convergence/local-minimizer research theorems reused or cited.
Boundary-reaction renormalized-energy existence and uniform expansion, infinite-dimensional compactness/recovery sequences, and the square-to-smooth-convex construction of the manuscript.
Periodic nonlocal rearrangement inequalities and equality-case classification for the three kernel classes.

Standard weak Harnack, boundary elliptic W2p bootstrap, smooth-domain trace localization, density and zero-trace kernel theorem; the boundary barrier and half-space trace Fourier steps themselves are supplied.

source_errata.decision: Use f(u)=exp(u) and put lambda outside f consistently, avoiding the source's local double-lambda ambiguity.
Nonnegative second variation is linearized/variational stability. Do not infer nonlinear heat-flow Lyapunov stability at a zero eigenvalue without additional hypotheses.
The scale-one arctangent layer has outward flux sin(pi u)/pi. Keep an explicit scale a; a=1/pi matches sin(pi u). This is independently differentiated rather than silently copied.
The second and third lines disagree on the first regular-part argument. Do not guess an original-paper correction; omit this formula and define W by the unambiguous energy limit (4.5).
Preserve manuscript 2025 in the abstract and forthcoming 2026 in the bibliography; do not promote the underlying boundary-reaction paper to formally published status.

The retrieved introductory prose has a Hardy coefficient inconsistent with its dimensional threshold. Use the independently proved sharp coefficient (n-2)^2/4, yielding n>=7 for u=1-r; no source typo is used as a premise.
Do not treat an HTML conversion/display date as the pinned version's submission date. Version identifiers and abstract metadata control source identity.
